sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector underperformed the aggregate, dragged by local names, but global semis like Samsung (+6.97%) and SK Hynix (+5.90%) surged on AI demand signals. Focus on GPSO (+14.01%) and TRON (+12.38%) as high-beta plays; the signal is NORMAL, suggesting no systemic risk—position for selective AI-linked hardware exposure in Indonesia's digital economy tailwind.

Urbanization and e-commerce penetration are creating durable demand for personal care and household products, benefiting local manufacturers with strong distribution networks.
Government policies supporting domestic manufacturing and raw material self-sufficiency are lowering input costs for consumer goods firms, enhancing margin stability.
sectors.ai: Indonesia consumer stocks rallied 0.67% today vs US -0.42%, led by AGAR (+24.75%) and BMBL (+9.68%), signaling domestic demand resilience. Focus on mid-cap FMCG and specialty retail names as structural tailwinds from rising middle-class consumption and urbanization persist. Maintain overweight on select food/beverage and personal care plays.

Biotech innovation cycles (ALNY) and orphan drug approvals provide asymmetric upside, but require careful timing given regulatory and reimbursement risks.
sectors.ai: Healthcare's modest decline masks strong divergence: Indonesia's WIRG (+9.26%) and RLCO (+4.80%) signal domestic demand resilience, while US laggards like ELV (+2.44%) and ISRG (+2.24%) reflect selective innovation plays. Favor Indonesia-focused names for structural growth, as US exposure remains vulnerable to policy headwinds.

Favor selective exposure to last-mile and cold-chain operators as e-commerce and food delivery volumes accelerate; avoid pure-play commodity haulers given global trade headwinds.
